notes: Closest match on mechanism (MEC-11, MEC-08). The Commission reports do not name MConnect or platform underuse: the 2025 report (text read) says only "interoperability between automated verification systems and state registries must still be strengthened", on asset declarations, which does echo the North Macedonian asset declaration items. The issue comes from the Court of Accounts performance audit: "only 6" of 11 sampled service providers connected, and connection "not a well-planned and organized process". What was tried: Law 142/2018 with an obligation to connect, then contravention fines and a ban on refusing service for documents available on the platform, effective 18 January 2021. Mixed: the audit reports a positive trend of use but limited connection. No current count of connected institutions found. CAUTION: ccrm.md returned 403 to the fetch tool, so the audit wording comes from search excerpts only, its date is unconfirmed (excerpts conflict) and the full report was not read; it may need manual acquisition, and may be in Romanian. Moldova is a less direct fit to test 1 than Montenegro.

Commission 2025: "The interoperability framework is also in place. There are more databases connected to the improved government service bus", with development "hampered by the fragmentation of responsibilities and mandates among institutions". Serbia is a case of wider connection, so it tests what raised use, not persisting low connection. Reform: a duty in the 2016 procedure law to exchange data from official records, plus the eZUP system, which ministry sources credit with 170 million+ items exchanged over the Government Service Bus in six years and 300 to 350 user bodies (the 350 is a search excerpt only). These are government self-reports; I found no State Audit Institution audit. Independent outcome is mixed: the WeBER monitor finds the once-only principle applied for sampled services except property registration, yet about 53 to 54% of citizens (the report gives both figures) said they had to submit documents already held by the state. Attribution to eZUP is unproven.

Closest EU wording. Commission 2025: "several challenges remain, particularly in consolidating digital services into a single e-government portal and improving interoperability and data exchange among institutions"; "The Law on administrative procedure has not been implemented consistently, particularly with regards to the once only principle"; "The integration of all public registers into the Unified System of Electronic Data Exchange has yet to be completed." It also notes "no effective collection of key data to monitor and incentivise public institutions". The mechanism leans to incomplete integration and implementation gap as well as low uptake. Reform: the JSERP exchange system, operating from 2023 with 18 institutions having access (NIFO 2024, search excerpt; the PDF text layer did not yield it). Outcome: WeBER reports only 19.9% of respondents reporting once-only in practice, though the wording of that figure is awkward and needs checking in the source. Confounder: the 2022 to 2023 cyberattack, which the Commission says delayed digital services. No State Audit Institution audit found. Useful as a slow or stalled case.

CLOSE CALL, not recommended. Connection is not the problem here: the audit office report (Albanian) cites 58 systems on the platform and other sources give 61 to 63, so the MKD mechanism of few institutions using the platform does not hold. Commission 2025 says e-Albania "enables interactions with several databases, and provides for pre-filled applications forms" and does not report underuse. What pushed use was channel closure (counters closed, online-only applications), but I found no independent evaluation of that step and sources disagree on its date. WeBER: half of surveyed citizens still report being asked for documents already held by the state, a useful once-only caution. The audit covers online services and AKSHI capacity, not platform uptake, and is in Albanian. Could replace Montenegro if the analyst wants a contrasting high-connection case. SIGMA 2024 Albania PDF returned 403, not read.

GSB exists and government claims strong interoperability and OOTS progress, but these are self-reports. I found no State Audit Office finding or independent evidence of uptake, in one English-language search each; a Croatian-language search was not run. Reputation is not evidence, so left out.

Found while looking for audit evidence in member states. Supreme Audit Office K23005: the basic registers concept "did not meet the increasing requirements", and systems create local copies of reference data rather than using it. A real audit with outcomes in English, but it concerns register transformation and spending in a much more mature system, not institutions failing to join a platform, and it is not a recent accession. Only worth a look as a supplementary audit reference.
RegiX: old State e-Government Agency figures only (65 registers, 25 administrations). No audit or outcome evidence found. Search was shallow; not excluded on substance.
